title: Information-Theoretic Channel Capacity of Human Feedback

original_idea.body:
# Channel Capacity of Human Feedback

**Problem:** We don't quantify how much true-value information a noisy preference channel can transmit.

**Direction:** Inject controlled label noise into synthetic-ground-truth preference pairs, run DPO, estimate mutual information as noise rises; estimate channel capacity.

**Why it matters:** Quantifies a fundamental RLHF limit. Synthetic data.

**Relevant context:** Open Problems in RLHF; arXiv:2509.19325.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Quantifying a fundamental RLHF limit is valuable but the chain to catastrophic-risk reduction is abstract.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Mutual-information estimation plus channel-capacity framing is intermediate, beyond a first-project beginner.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused capacity-estimation; synthetic-value construction and MI estimation are dependencies.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Synthetic data, small fine-tunes; foundational limit labs underinvest in.

low_compute.reasoning: Small synthetic DPO runs; one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Information-theoretic framing of preference learning may be partly open though related theory exists.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Channel-capacity framing of preference learning may be partly open.
